title: Check yourself: Least privilege, blocking hooks, sandboxes and secrets

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An agent reads web pages and can send mail to any address. Which change best reduces what an injected instruction can do?

options.text: Add a sentence to the system prompt that forbids sending any mail
options.says: Ruled out because "Whatever the injected text asks for, the agent can do only what its grants allow", and a sentence in a prompt is not a grant.

options.text: Screen each page with a pattern list before the agent sees the text
options.says: Ruled out because the grants stay the same after a screen, and the page says to "run tools in sandboxed environments, and scope permissions as narrowly as possible".

options.text: Ask the model to explain why it wants to send a message at all
options.says: Ruled out because an explanation from the model changes no grant, and the page says "don't give Claude access to secrets it doesn't need".

options.text: Limit the tool to a short list of approved recipient domains
options.says: The table gives the narrow answer for actions: mail goes "only to listed domains", so a hostile instruction gets at most those recipients.

questions.stem: A deny entry for `Bash(git push *)` does not stop the agent's `git -C . push origin main`. Which change closes that gap?

options.text: A second deny entry for each other spelling that comes up
options.says: Ruled out because "a push behind `&&` or inside `sh -c` is a different string", so every new spelling is a new gap, and a list can never be complete.

options.text: A hook that parses the line and checks the real subcommand
options.says: The page says a deny rule "matches the text as written", so `git -C . push` is a different string, and "A hook can parse the command into its parts".

options.text: A line in the memory file that forbids any push to the remote
options.says: Ruled out because "A memory line asks, and a hook enforces."

options.text: An allow entry for `git -C . push` that outranks the deny entry
options.says: Ruled out because deny rules "are checked before everything else", so an allow entry outranks nothing and would only approve the push.

questions.stem: A team turns on the Bash isolation boundary with an empty domain list and assumes the WebFetch tool is blocked too. Why is that wrong?

options.text: An empty list means no limit, so every domain stays reachable
options.says: Ruled out because network access goes "through a proxy on your machine that checks each host against your allowed domains, which start empty", so an empty list allows nothing from the shell.

options.text: The fetch tool runs inside the boundary, but its proxy lets that call through
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude's file tools, MCP servers, and hooks run outside it", and the web tools "follow permission rules instead".

options.text: It covers shell commands only, so built-in web access follows permission rules
options.says: The page says "The sandbox covers shell commands only", and that the built-in file and web tools "follow permission rules instead", so `allowedDomains` "doesn't limit WebFetch".

options.text: Only MCP servers sit outside the boundary, and every built-in tool runs within it
options.says: Ruled out because the built-in file and web tools "follow permission rules instead", so they are outside it too.
